title: Obtaining patient-derived cancer organoid cultures via fine-needle aspiration
protocol: Attach a sterile 25-gauge beveled needle to a sterile 10 mL luer-lock syringe and insert into a syringe holder.
Transfer specimen to a sterile petri dish within a laminar flow biosafety cabinet if using surgical tissue.
Perform FNA in vivo in a procedure room with sterile technique.
Immobilize the specimen/nodule with sterile-gloved fingers or sterile forceps.
Insert the needle with the syringe holder perpendicular to the specimen/nodule.
Apply backward pressure to the syringe using the syringe holder.
Rapidly agitate back and forth in a “saw-like” motion within the specimen at a rate of 2–3 strokes per second.
Perform 10–20 forward strokes (excursions) for one “needle pass”.
Reangle the needle slightly with each excursion to sample in a fan shape.
Ensure material is visible in the needle hub before stopping agitation.
Do not allow the needle to protrude from the opposite side of the specimen at any point.
Release suction before removing the needle from the specimen.
Rinse the needle in 20 mL of sterile, pre-warmed RPMI or DMEM in a 50 mL conical tube.
Expel the needle contents into the conical tube.
Repeat rinsing the needle 2-3 times.
Dispose of the syringe and needle in an appropriate sharps container.
Collect cells via fine needle aspiration (FNA).
Centrifuge the FNA material at 340 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Resuspend the pellet in Complete Media using 600 μL and divide into two 300 μL aliquots if both culture methods are to be used.
Plate half of the cells in semi-solid culture in a 24-well ultra-low attachment plate using one of the prepared 300 μL aliquots.
Resuspend the remaining cell half for disc culture in another 300 μL Complete Media and plate it in a 6-well plate with 75% Matrigel disc culture.
Pipette 300 μL of the FNA cell suspension with 5% Matrigel in complete media and additional 2% FBS.
Mix the pipetted solution thoroughly.
Pipette 550 μL of the mixed cell suspension into a 24-well low-attachment plate using a figure 8 motion while gently expelling the cell suspension.
Place the cells in the incubator.
Replenish each well with 200 μL of fresh complete media, 5% Matrigel, and 2% FBS dropwise weekly.
Passage cells as needed.
Pipette and mix 300 μL of the FNA cell suspension with 75% Matrigel and 25% complete media.
Add three 50 μL drops (disc) to each well of a pre-warmed 6-well plate.
Alternatively, plate a single 150–200 μL disc per well of the 6-well plate.
Place the plate in a tissue culture incubator for 10 min to allow the Matrigel to solidify.
Cover cells with warmed complete media by slowly pipetting the media down the side of the well until the discs are completely covered (~2.5 mL).
Place cells back in the incubator.
Replace media every 2–3 days by aspirating off the old media and replacing it with pre-warmed complete media.
Freeze the disc down following the freezing cells protocol once cells have undermined the disc.
Add 2 mL of 20°C–25°C complete media to each well after removing disc.
Passage cells from the 6-well plate to a T75 flask when media needs replaced or replenished more often than twice a week or when organoids are harvested for experimental use.
Resuspend and aliquot organoids after centrifugation.
Pipette 700 μL of the resuspended organoid suspension into a new conical tube for replating when performing a 1:4 passage.
Transfer the remaining 2,100 μL to separate tubes for freezing or other uses.
Draw up and expel a small amount of organoid suspension in a circular motion with a P1000 pipette to break up Matrigel/organoids.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 340 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate off the supernatant from the pelleted cells.
Resuspend the pelleted cells in complete media.
Pipette out the desired amount of the resuspended cell suspension and replate following step 12b of the cell growth protocol.
Remove media from disc culture wells.
Add 1 mL ice-cold PBS to each well for disc removal.
Scrape discs gently off the plate with a cell scraper.
Use pipetted ice-cold PBS to break apart discs and collect them into a microfuge tube.
Centrifuge cells at 340 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Remove PBS and Matrigel overlying the pellet after centrifugation.
Wash the cell pellet gently with 1 mL of cold PBS.
Centrifuge again at 340 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate off all the media from the cells in a 6-well plate.
Add 1 mL of trypsin to each well and incubate at 37°C for 3 min.
Pipette trypsinized cells from each well into a conical tube with 20 mL of DMEM or RPMI.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 340 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C and aspirate off the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets in 1 mL of complete media then transfer to a T75 flask containing 14 mL of complete media.
Rock the T75 flask back and forth until the bottom is covered with cell suspension.
Place the T75 flask in the incubator.
Aspirate off the media from the cells.
Pipette 1 mL of 4°C PBS directly onto the disc in each well.
Use a cell scraper to gently scrape off any remaining disc.
Pipette the cell suspension into a 1.5 mL microfuge tube and pipette up and down several times to dissolve the Matrigel.
Follow relevant steps in the Passaging Cells protocol and save the remaining cell suspension.
Pipette 20 μL into a hemocytometer to count the number of cells.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 340 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate off the supernatant and resuspend in complete DMEM.
For disc and semi-solid culture, deposit approximately 2 wells per cryovial.
For 2D culture, deposit 300,000–1,000,000 cells per cryovial.
Pipette 700 μL of cell suspension into each appropriately labeled cryovial.
Pipette 200 μL of FBS into each cryovial.
Pipette 100 μL of DMSO into a cryovial.
Screw the cap on tightly and invert 2–3 times.
Place directly into a Mr. Frosty.
Tighten the lid on the Mr. Frosty and place directly into a −80°C freezer.
After a week in the −80°C freezer, transfer cells to a liquid nitrogen freezer at or below −130°C for longer storage.
Preheat water bath to 37°C.
Pipette 20 mL of media into a 50 mL conical tube and warm to ~24°C.
Obtain cryovial with cells.
Place cryovial in water bath.
Incubate for 1 minute then check if it has thawed.
If not fully thawed, check again in 15–30 seconds intervals until thawed completely.
Once thawed, pipette contents from cryovial into the media from step 28.
Rinse the cryovial with 1,000 μL of the media and pipette it back into the conical tube.
Screw the conical tube lid tightly and invert to ensure adequate mixing.
Centrifuge at 340 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate off the supernatant.
